text:
marco: quick thread to align on private deploy roadmap slice for customer-managed networking + upgrade continuity. field pressure increasing for installs that must keep egress IPs stable and for upgrades that cannot spike support load.
anya: agreed. we heard this from three pilots last month. want to land a minimal public flow we can ship as opt-in in Q2.
devon: engineering reality check: two main pieces: 1) egress pinning (don’t churn SNAT addresses during node churn/rolling upgrades) and 2) non-disruptive operator upgrades (CRD migration + schema compatibility + graceful control-plane handover). both touch packaging and runtime.
marco: proposal for roadmap slices: 
- Handshake API v1 (installer + netops): explicit pre-install handshake where customer provides egress-preserve intent and network owner verifies. UX + audit events.
- Egress-pin mode (runtime/CNI shim): operate in "host-nat" mode where we avoid recreating node-level SNAT addresses during upgrades.
- Operator rolling lanes: operator supports staged control-plane updates with live CRD adapters & health gated rollbacks.
- Pilot runbook + fast support path: runbook + dedicated pilot support hours for banks/regulators.
sam: timeline ballpark (parallel work): 
- Handshake API v1: 2w for schema + UX + docs; 1w integration tests.
- Egress-pin mode (spike + MVP): 3-5w (spike 1w, implement 2-4w, tests 1w)
- Rolling operator lanes: 5-7w (includes CRD adapters + canary controller)
- Runbook + pilot: 1-2w once features exist
ops-bot: CI: packaging-e2e job failing on operator-rolling-test 91A https://ci.internal/packaging-e2e/1245 A timeout on canary probe
anya: okay we should accept some overlap but define minimal viable shipping (MVS) per slice so field knows what counts as "shippable".
devon: suggested MVS: 
- Handshake API v1: installer accepts "egressKeep=true" flag; installer emits audit event and writes handshake manifest to /var/lib/redwood/handshake.json; integration test with a netops mock. validation by 2 pilot customers.
- Egress-pin mode: cluster restart + operator upgrade preserves advertised outbound IP as seen by an external echo service (automated test) AND docs with iptables/snattips.
- Operator rolling lanes: automated 3-step canary (10% -> 50% -> 100%) with health gates (request latency, error rate, CRD migration success) and automatic rollback hook. pilot pass required.
- Security: threat model reviewed, KMS interactions unchanged, logging/audit preserved.
marco: low-friction mitigations for customers waiting: provide a "network-handshake" template + Terraform example and offer short-term managed cutover where RD engineering handles the first install.
anya: also offer a fallback proxy shim (lightweight NAT box) customers can deploy inline for immediate IP stability. note: increases ops footprint and requires network ops signoff.
devon: open engineering risks: 
- cloud-proxy edge cases when customer uses NAT gateway pools (multiple egress IPs)
- CNI choice: some CNIs aggressively reallocate pod/host addresses on restart; need explicit tests across Calico, Cilium and host-network installs
- CRD migrations that change versioned schemas must be reversible or have an adapter layer
sam: priorities (vote): 
- P0: Handshake API + Egress-pin MVP + runbook (customer-facing, pilot-ready)
- P1: Rolling operator lanes (canary controller + rollback automation)
- P2: Fallback NAT proxy + advanced ipam integrations
- P3: BGP automation + managed peering orchestration
anya: +1 P0 first. banks need a predictable deliverable. devon: agree but ask that we run a 1-wk CRD migration spike while egress-pin is in progress so we don't end up blocked.
marco: decision: P0 first, start parallel 1-wk CRD migration spike. owners: handshake API = @anya, egress-pin = @devon, runbook/pilot coordination = @sam. target: internal pilot in 5 weeks, external pilot invites week 6.
devon: I'll draft the CNI shim design and include a smoke test: external-echo-check script that curls httpbin from each node pre/post upgrade and verifies single stable IP.
anya: I'll add API schema & example CLI: 
```
redwood-installer install --profile private \ 
  --preserve-egress=true \ 
  --egress-owner-contact "netops@example.com" \ 
  --handshake-token-file /tmp/handshake.sig
```
sam: I'll assemble the pilot runbook and coordinate with AE field. also adding a short "what to expect" doc for customers (latency during canary, rollback semantics).
ops-bot: Note: packaging-e2e scheduled daily on branch preserve-egress until pilot.
marco: action items recap: 
- anya: push handshake API PR w/ schema & docs (due in 4d)
- devon: CNI shim RFC + smoke test + initial impl (spike 1w, MVP 4w) (first draft in 5d)
- sam: runbook draft & pilot outreach (due in 7d)
- ops-bot: run packaging-e2e daily and surface failures
marco: any other blockers? security signoff timeline?
anya: we need Sec review queued; I'll request review now and aim for signoff within pilot window.
devon: also request perf team to watch canary tail latency; constraint: upgrades should not add >15% p99 for control-plane proxied calls.
sam: field note: two customers already approved pilot terms if we can guarantee a rollback window and support SLA. I'll add them to pilot list.
marco: great. will put these items on the roadmap board and schedule a 30m sync next Mon to review handshake PR and smoke-test results.
